evidence.text:
山公舉阮咸爲吏部郎目曰淸眞寡欲萬物不能移
也
(為正始名士阮嗣宗嵇叔夜山/宏以夏侯太初何平叔王輔嗣)

judgment.explanation: 嵇康 is the subject of the passage, described in terms of his physical appearance (身長七尺八寸風姿特秀). The candidate 嵇康 matches the canonical name directly and the Liu annotation confirms 康長七尺 referring to the same person.

康 in the Liu annotation 康别傳 refers to 嵇康 by his personal name. The annotation text 康别傳曰康長七尺 directly parallels the main text's description of 嵇康's height, and the semantic record confirms coreference with the full name 嵇康 in the main text.

review.explanation: The surface form 嵇康 appears verbatim in the main text (sfh1-ev-14-rongzhi-005-main) as the opening subject of the passage describing a person of seven chi eight cun stature with exceptional bearing. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-14-rongzhi-005-liu-annotation-001) also references 康 as an abbreviation of 嵇康 in the context of his physical description. The canonical name match is direct and the contextual description (physical appearance, height) aligns with the known biographical details of 嵇康. No contradicting evidence exists.

The single character 康 in the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-14-rongzhi-005-liu-annotation-001) appears within the phrase 康别传曰, which is a standard abbreviated reference to 嵇康's biography (嵇康别传). The main text (sfh1-ev-14-rongzhi-005-main) explicitly names 嵇康 as the subject, and the annotation directly comments on that same person's physical description. The abbreviation is unambiguous in this context, and the coreference chain with the full name 嵇康 and style name 嵇叔夜 is well-supported.

The surface form 山公 appears in the main text (sfh1-ev-14-rongzhi-005-main) in the phrase 山公曰嵇叔夜之為人也, where 山公 is a well-established contextual title for 山濤 (Shan Tao). The alias registry evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-7c0faeacadbe07ae49f2) confirms 山公 as an alias for 山濤 in the context of the Shishuo Xinyu. The passage has 山公 commenting on 嵇康's character, which is consistent with the historical relationship between Shan Tao and Ji Kang as members of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. No contradicting evidence exists.

The surface form 嵇叔夜 appears in the main text (sfh1-ev-14-rongzhi-005-main) in the phrase 山公曰嵇叔夜之為人也, where 嵇叔夜 is the surname-plus-courtesy-name form for 嵇康 (Ji Kang, courtesy name Shuye). The alias registry evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-164cc89303043c984fe3) confirms 嵇叔夜 as an alias for 嵇康. The main text explicitly names 嵇康 as the subject at the opening, and 嵇叔夜 is used as his style name in the same passage, making the identity unambiguous. No contradicting evidence exists.
